project.name: @kehto/rate-limit
project.summary: Optional caps on how often a napplet (sandboxed iframe app) may act: a steady per-minute budget plus a startup burst limit, tighter for background napplets. Nothing is limited unless the host builds a limiter and passes it in. An older, retained policy model sits under its own legacy entry for hosts still migrating.

nodes.label: Action caps
nodes.summary: The current cap on how often each napplet may act: checks one action against its budget, and the host builds a cap object that remembers the counts.

nodes.label: Legacy policy
nodes.summary: The older per-napplet policy model kept for hosts that have not moved to scoped approvals yet: rules, content matching, default limits and a saved settings container, which now hands its counting to the current action caps.

nodes.label: Tests
nodes.summary: Automatic checks for both the current limiter and the legacy policy model.

nodes.label: Build settings
nodes.summary: How the package and its legacy entry are bundled for publishing.

steps.note: The host builds a cap object from its chosen settings and passes in who is acting, what operation, whether the napplet is in focus and the current time.
The pure check takes from that napplet's budget and startup allowance and says allow, flag or block, returning the updated counts to keep.
An older host passes an observation to the legacy evaluator, which applies its per-napplet rules first.
The counting itself is handed to the current action caps, so both paths share one counting method.

tour.title: Action caps
tour.note: A small, pure cap on how often each napplet may act. Hosts opt in by building one; importing the package installs nothing.

tour.title: The legacy model
tour.note: Kept for migration only. Its rules and settings still work, but counting goes through the current limiter.

tour.title: Where the two meet
tour.note: The legacy check calls into the current action caps rather than keeping a second counter.
